title: Are splay trees dynamically optimal?
question: Fix n ordered keys and an access sequence X. In the root-BST model, an access is served by rotations until its key is at the root; its cost is one plus the number of rotations. Let OPT(X) minimize total cost over offline executions, allowing an optimal initial tree. Is there a universal constant C such that, for every initial splay tree T₀ and every X, $\mathrm{cost}_{\mathrm{splay}}(X;T_0)\le C(\mathrm{OPT}(X)+n)$? The additive term allows an arbitrary initial configuration.

title: Multipass pairing heaps: logarithmic amortized delete-min — resolved
question: Does the standard multipass pairing heap satisfy the following bound? For every valid operation sequence starting with no heaps, let D be the number of delete-min operations, Q the number of all other operations, and N the maximum size of any heap during the sequence. The total number of key comparisons and constant-time pointer operations is at most C[Q + D log₂(N+2)] for a universal C. Allowed operations are make-heap, insert, find-min, meld and delete-min. The answer is yes, as a consequence of Sinnamon and Tarjan’s theorem.
